newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur barges pushed up by sole buyer.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur barges pushed up by sole buyer.

text.p: NWE high sulphur barge prices rose on Wednesday on the back of concerted buying by a single purchaser but other fuel oil product markets were quiet.
High sulphur barges were heard traded up from Tuesday's $85 fob ARA level to $89 with offers still being heard at $89 before lunch.
Some other business was done in Rotterdam and Antwerp.
Traders said there was little solid support to the market, although bunker interest was good.
They speculated that the buying was tied to a medium-sized cargo sale.
Portugal's state electricity company EdP's 25,000 tonne high sulphur buy tender was heard awarded to Portugese refiner Petrogal, an outcome widely expected in the market.
The price was heard to be $8.55 above the two fob high sulphur means. The option for the second cargo was not taken up by the buyer.
High and low sulphur cargo markets were very quiet ahead of the Easter break with prices stable. Low sulphur availabilities were said to be tight in the prompt period but good from mid to late April.
